title: Tiered Elevation Roadmap and SLA Samples
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact, action-first playbook for Customer Success teams running QBRs and renewal conversations focused on tiered elevation (hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) and premium SLA add-ons. Goal: enable a 6-week expansion program that moves production-critical customers to Dedicated capacity or Private deployments with clear technical validation, cost/benefit messaging, and an execution cadence that aligns GTM, solutions engineering, and finance.

Quick summary (1 line):
A repeatable QBR + 6-week technical & commercial sprint to convert high-usage customers to contract commitments for Dedicated or Private, or to add premium SLA tiers.

When to use this doc (signals):
- Monthly token spend > $15k and growth rate > 20% MoM
- Sustained p95 latency breaches vs SLA targets (hosted) or variable tail latency during peak windows
- Frequent KV cache misses or high re-generation rates (cost inefficiency)
- Data residency, compliance, or VPC requirements called out by legal/security
- Customer asks for predictable throughput/cost (e.g., RPS guarantees, reserved slots)
- Platform/infra requests in support tickets: more predictable latency, isolated workloads, or DDoS concerns

Cohort segmentation for outreach (examples):
- Warm candidates: sustained spend + engaged SEs in last 30 days
- Technical champions identified: has infra or platform engineer in QBR invite
- Executive economics: churn risk if not converted (finance signaled)

QBR agenda template (45–60 minutes):
- 5m — Welcome + objective for QBR (this meeting is about capacity & risk reduction)
- 10m — Current state: usage trends, token economics, latency/cost hotspots (SE presents)
- 10m — Business impact: product features enabled by scale, revenue ops impact (CS)
- 10m — Elevation options overview: Dedicated vs Private vs SLA add-ons (solutioning)
- 5m — Live technical checklist & readiness signals (quick go/no-go)
- 5–10m — Commercial framing + pricing example (finance/CS)
- 5m — Next steps and owner/commitments

Technical readiness checklist (to be completed by SE before escalation):
- Baseline metrics snapshot: tokens/day, peak RPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV hit rate
- Model variants in use + typical generation seq lengths (avg, 95th)
- Current retry/regenerate rates and root causes
- Data residency constraints, encryption/KMS requirements, IP allowlists
- Integration footprint: SDKs used, webhook patterns, streaming vs sync calls
- Traffic shaping needs (burst windows, predictable traffic curves)
- Canary & rollback appetite: can customer tolerate short rollbacks?
- Any 3rd-party compliance evidence required (SOC2, ISO, etc.)

Risk & mitigation mapping (talking points for SEs):
- Risk: Performance variability on shared pool -> Mitigation: Dedicated pool with routing policy + autoscaling buffer
- Risk: Cost unpredictability -> Mitigation: Reserved capacity commit + committed discounts + quota controls
- Risk: Data egress / residency -> Mitigation: Private VPC or on-prem pack + KMS integration
- Risk: Feature compatibility (plugins/tooling) -> Mitigation: Validate runtime kernels and model variants in pre-prod instance

Pricing vignette (example numbers, adjust per customer):
- Current hosted spend: $18k/month (avg) -> projected 3-month run rate $21k with growth
- Dedicated proposal: base reserved $12k/month + overage @ $6/token-unit -> net expected unit cost drop ~18% for steady state
- Private one-time onboarding & infra fee: $45k + $8k/month platform fee (for small infra bundle)
- SLA add-on: +15% of base monthly for 99.9% uptime commitments and priority escalation
- Include a 12-month committed-case and a 6-month pilot path (pilot: 20% discount, limited SLA)

ROI framing (short bullets to use with exec):
- Predictable cost: reduce per-token variance and cap worst-case spend
- Feature velocity: internal teams can rely on stable latency for production rollouts
- Reduced support ops: fewer regen calls and lower incident MTTR
- Revenue enablement: ability to roll out synchronous features (autocomplete, search rerank) with guaranteed perf

6-week escalation sprint (operational runbook):
Week 0 (prep): gather metrics, schedule QBR, identify stakeholders
Week 1: QBR + decision (pilot vs commit) + SE technical scoping
Week 2: Provision pilot Dedicated/Private environment (SE + infra)
Week 3: Migration validation & perf testing (load tests, KV caching config)
Week 4: Customer QA & integration fixes
Week 5: Commercial signoff & contract work (sales + finance)
Week 6: Go-live pilot -> monitor, weekly ops sync -> conversion to committed reserved capacity if criteria met

Success criteria for pilot conversion (example):
- p95 latency <= target (as agreed) for 7 consecutive days
- Cost per 1k tokens <= target threshold agreed in QBR
- No P1/P2 incidents related to inference in 14 days
- Customer adoption: x% of traffic routed to new tier or y new product features launched

Customer-facing templates (short):
- QBR invite subject: "QBR: Capacity & SLA review — [Customer] / Redwood"
- Exec summary blurb to include in QBR deck: "We recommend a staged Dedicated deployment to stabilize latency and reduce per-token cost. Pilot path proposed: 6 weeks, low-risk, with clear go/no-go criteria."
- Follow-up email snippet (post-QBR): "Thanks for the time today — attached are the pilot steps, technical checklist, and pricing vignette. If you confirm pilot by EOD Friday we can provision week 2. Owner: SE [name]."

Internal playbook checklist for CS/SE/Sales handoff (quick):
- [ ] SE completes technical readiness sheet (link to CONPLAT-782)
- [ ] CS prepares cost model and sends pricing vignette
- [ ] Sales draft term sheet for pilot (legal loop-in)
- [ ] Infra tickets opened for Dedicated/Private provisioning
- [ ] Escalation contact list shared with customer (SRE on-call)

Objection handling snippets (short):
- "We’re worried about lock-in": explain routing fallbacks + ability to pin model versions + exit runway (data export & rollback)
- "We don’t want to pay more": show unit-economic comparison + cost predictability benefits + pilot discount
- "We need compliance evidence": attach SOC2 artifacts + KMS architecture diagram + offer Private deployment checklist

Dashboards & artifacts to include in QBR deck:
- Token spend trends (monthly + 90d)
- Peak RPS heatmap (hour-of-day)
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) pre/post pilot
- KV cache hit-rate and regeneration counts
- Incident timeline (if any) and MTTR improvements expected

Notes to self / things to iterate on (open items):
- Insert short 1-page visual comparing Dedicated vs Private (engineering to supply asset)
- Create a one-click provisioning playbook for pilots (RE: infra tickets and permissions)
- Standardize pilot T&Cs for 3 pilot sizes (small/med/large)
- Need a templated Pricing Calculator sheet (Finance) that takes spend, expected growth, and shows Dedicated vs Hosted NPV

References / links (placeholders):
- Pilot provisioning runbook: CONPLAT-782 (internal)
- Ticket template: CS-341 (Linear)
- Sample contract terms PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-onboarding/pull/88

Appendix: Short checklist for SE performance test (copy into runbook):
- Run 10k synthetic requests across 3 seq-len profiles (short, medium, long)
- Validate KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior
- Confirm model variant parity for outputs (sanity checks)
- Run 48h soak test at average expected load + 2x burst window for 30min
